column1: # clues.tsv for ft_atoi_base — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

A character's digit value is not its ASCII code. For a character to be a digit at all it has to appear somewhere in base — so what does the place it appears tell you about the value it stands for? Are you deriving each character's value from the base you were given, rather than assuming the characters are '0'..'9'?

Where should the conversion stop? The instant you meet a character that does not appear anywhere in the base, what should you do with the rest of the string? Are you leaning on isdigit or a fixed 0-9 test instead of "is this character in the base"?

A run of leading '+'/'-' may hold more than one sign. What decides the final sign — the first one, the last one, or how many '-' you saw? And once the signs are consumed, does normal digit reading resume from there?

The base must pass strict checks before any digit is read. How many distinct characters does it need at the very least? May a character repeat? May it contain a whitespace, a '+' or a '-'? If the base fails any of these tests, what must the function hand back without parsing the string at all?
